scope: All 147 stories tagged ARC-AID, ARC-EQUITY, ARC-PORTAL-BREACH, ARC-CONTRACTS or ARC-RUMORS (days -45 to 119), read in day order against the public record, canon, characters, outlets and the restricted and quantity rules. Focus: relief and FEMA aid, the equity analysis, the account takeovers, emergency contracts, and rumors and fact-checks.

findings.old: A debris hauler and a fuel supplier hired after Rafael face a county audit, a Navy suspension and a federal inspector general review. Both dispute the findings against them.
findings.new: A debris hauler and a fuel supplier hired after Rafael face a county audit and a Navy suspension in separate matters, as a federal inspector general reviews storm contracts. Both defend their work.
findings.reason: No review has made findings (the body says none has); the IG review never named either company; before day 114 the two firms should read as separate matters, not a pair.
findings.resolution: Verified resolved by another reviewer's fix (checked 2026-11-08).

findings.old: two companies that won emergency work in its aftermath are under review by the county, the Navy and a federal inspector general.
findings.new: two companies that won emergency work in its aftermath face separate reviews by the county and the Navy, and a federal inspector general is reviewing storm contracts in the region.
findings.reason: The lead puts both companies under IG review, but the same story says the IG announcement did not name specific companies (PUB-090). Keep the two cases separate before day 114.

findings.old: and have since come under county, Navy and federal review.
findings.new: and have since come under separate county and Navy reviews.
findings.reason: The IG review (PUB-090) never named either company, and the story itself later says it is unclear whether the searches connect to it.

findings.old: executed court-authorized search warrants today at two locations in Corpus Christi
findings.new: executed court-authorized search warrants today in Corpus Christi
findings.reason: PUB-094 says only 'the offices' of the two firms. Ground truth registers both firms at one address, so 'two locations' adds a detail that clashes with the answer key. The FBI spokesman would not volunteer it.

findings.old: FALSE. The Ledger's report concerns
findings.new: NO EVIDENCE. The Ledger's report concerns
findings.reason: The reasoning ('the report says nothing about FEMA payments') supports 'no evidence', not 'false'. On Jan. 6 (PUB-098) a federal filing says accounts tied to the contractors received $3.9M in diverted aid, so a FALSE verdict on day 79 would read as debunking what the court record later alleges. The headline already says 'doesn't show'.

findings.old: If your aid payment never showed up, here's what to know.
findings.new: The filing does not say how the aid was diverted. If your aid payment never showed up, here's what to know.
findings.reason: The headline and body treat the $3.9M as the hijacked deposits, but PUB-098 gives no mechanism. NWS-P114-01 and NWS-P116-01 say how the aid was diverted is not public, so keep the allegation as the record states it.

findings.old: "We'll cooperate fully with any review," said Nadia Kerr, Quellmar's operations manager. "All product we delivered meets specifications."
findings.new: "We'll cooperate fully with any review," said Nadia Kerr, Quellmar's operations manager, who repeated that all product the company delivered met specifications.
findings.reason: Same quote word for word as NWS-P075-01 and NWS-P079-02. This paraphrases the repeat instead of presenting it as a fresh quote.

findings.old: bills at 2.3 times county estimates
findings.new: billed tonnage at 2.3 times county estimates
findings.reason: 'Bills at 2.3 times' can be read as dollars, the misreading Harborline itself rates MISLEADING in NWS-P079-03. The record compares tonnage (PUB-088).

findings.old: Survey estimates are not exact counts, and invoices reflect what a contractor says it hauled.
findings.new: A survey estimate is not a count, and an invoice is the contractor's own tally of what it hauled.
findings.reason: Same sentence word for word as NWS-P078-02 (same outlet, two days earlier). This rewords it.

findings.old: Oct. 25: The station's backup generator fails during a power interruption. Power is restored; the cause is placed under review.
findings.new: Oct. 25: The station says its backup generator failed during a power interruption. Power was restored; the cause is under review.
findings.reason: Oct. 25 is the day the station disclosed the failure (PUB-065; NWS-P075-01: 'On Oct. 25, the station said...'), not a known failure date.

findings.old: the county's own aerial and satellite surveys
findings.new: the county's own drone and satellite surveys
findings.reason: PUB-088 and every other story say 'drone and satellite surveys'.

findings.old: Most came from low-income neighborhoods near the bay.
findings.new: Most came from low-lying neighborhoods near the bay.
findings.reason: PUB-026 says most 911 calls came from low-lying neighborhoods. Restating it as 'low-income' changes the public fact and moves toward the hidden tract-level split.

findings.old: the figure lands hard in places where families got half their share
findings.new: the figure lands hard in neighborhoods that got about half their share
findings.reason: PUB-091 is about neighborhoods' aid dollars at about half their share of residents, not about what families got. Keep 'about'.

findings.old: It doesn't answer why help took twice as long to arrive in the first place.
findings.new: It doesn't answer why help took more than twice as long to arrive in the first place.
findings.reason: The finding is 2.1 times. The researcher who produced it would not round down.

findings.old: and a researcher tied them to a lookalike site
findings.new: and a researcher found coordinated rumor posts pointing to the same lookalike site
findings.reason: PUB-054: the researcher linked the rumor posts to the lookalike site that the phishing emails already used. The emails were not newly tied to it.

findings.old: register for evacuation assistance with the county well before June
findings.new: register for evacuation assistance through 2-1-1 well before June
findings.reason: Earlier coverage (NWS-M045-02, NWS-M029-01, NWS-M012-01) sets up the state STEAR registry through 2-1-1, not a county list.

findings.new: Rewrite to a distinct angle or cut. As written, it repeats NWS-P069-01 from the day before: same reporter and outlet, same Thanksgiving-week feature on Rosa's daily deposit check, her pending application and her leak, and Whitfield's Thursday dinner, with no reference back. If kept, make it a true follow-up (for example other renters on Whitfield's list, or what applicants are hearing from the helpline) and say Elizondo registered on the first day, Nov. 13, not 'that first week'.
findings.reason: Near-duplicate of the previous day's story by the same reporter in the same outlet.
findings.resolution: Handled by rewrite-W1/W2 (public record corrected and stories rewritten).

findings.new: Rewrite as a real follow-up or cut. It repeats NWS-P092-02 (Harborline, same producer, the previous afternoon) almost point for point: ask for ID, no fee, no password, check your deposit, call the helpline. The headline is also near-identical. A follow-up could cover what papers to have ready for a door visit, or how people who already applied check their status, and should refer to Wednesday's story. Also fix 'A threat researcher later tied those emails to a lookalike site' (PUB-054 links the rumor posts to the site the emails already used).
findings.reason: Near-duplicate service piece from the same outlet on consecutive days.
findings.resolution: Handled by rewrite-W1/W2 (public record corrected and stories rewritten).

findings.old: In low-income neighborhoods near the bay, they remain about 40% above.
findings.new: Near the bay, in low-income neighborhoods, visits are still running about 40% above normal.
findings.reason: Same dek sentence word for word as NWS-P045-01 (Ledger, same day).
findings.resolution: Verified resolved by another reviewer's fix (checked 2026-11-08).

findings.old: Health officials have not said what is behind the gap.
findings.new: The health district has not yet said what is driving the difference.
findings.reason: Same body sentence word for word as NWS-P045-01 (same day).

findings.reason: In NWS-P003-04 and NWS-P055-02, Rosa got her first water and rice in person in the hall's line on Sept. 17. As written, the bike delivery reads as her first help.
